name: PCM1780DBQR
title: PCM1780, PCM1781, PCM1782: 24-bit, 192 kHz stereo delta-sigma audio DAC
summary: A stereo 24-bit audio DAC on one 5 V supply in a 16-pin SSOP, built on an enhanced multilevel delta-sigma modulator with a 4x/8x oversampling interpolation filter. It takes sampling rates from 5 kHz to 200 kHz and detects the system clock ratio, 128 fS to 1152 fS, by itself. PCM1780 and PCM1782 are set up over a three-wire serial port (attenuation, soft mute, de-emphasis, filter rolloff, data format, zero flags); PCM1782 has open-drain zero flags. PCM1781 is set by four pins. PCM1780 shares its pinout with the eight-channel PCM1680.

circuits.title: Basic connection, PCM1780 and PCM1782
circuits.description: The minimum set of parts round a software-controlled PCM1780 or PCM1782. The supply pin gets a 0.1 µF ceramic and a 10 µF electrolytic to ground; VCOM gets a 10 µF electrolytic to ground. Each analog output leaves through a 4.7 µF to 10 µF electrolytic coupling capacitor into an external post low-pass filter. The four audio-side inputs (SCK, DATA, BCK, LRCK) each come in through a 22 Ω to 100 Ω series resistor; the three mode-control lines and both zero flags are wired directly, with no parts. Pins 9 and 10 are left open.
notes: The same connections serve the PCM1782; its zero flags are open drain.

circuits.title: Basic connection, PCM1781
circuits.description: The hardware-controlled PCM1781 with the same supply, VCOM and output parts as the PCM1780 circuit: 0.1 µF ceramic plus 10 µF electrolytic on VCC, 10 µF electrolytic on VCOM, 4.7 µF to 10 µF electrolytic coupling into a post low-pass filter on each output, and 22 Ω to 100 Ω series resistors on SCK, DATA, BCK and LRCK. FMT, DEMP0, DEMP1 and MUTE are driven directly as logic levels; the common zero flag ZEROA goes back to the mute control. TEST and NC (pin 10) are left open.

circuits.title: VCOM biasing a single-supply filter stage
circuits.description: One output channel (VOUTL or VOUTR) feeds a second-order multiple-feedback low-pass filter built on half of an OPA2353 running from VCC alone. VCOM, decoupled by 10 µF, sets the op amp's non-inverting input, so the stage sits at mid-supply. R1 into the C2 node, R2 back from the output, R3 into the inverting input and C1 from output to inverting input set the response; gain is –R2/R1, shown as –1. The output passes through R4 and a coupling capacitor, with R5 to ground, to the line output.
notes: The input is either output, VOUTL or VOUTR.

circuits.title: VCOM buffered by a voltage follower
circuits.description: Where VCOM has to bias several nodes, an OPA337 wired as a unity-gain follower buffers it. VCOM keeps its 10 µF capacitor to ground and drives the follower's non-inverting input; the output, tied back to the inverting input, is the buffered VCOM. The op amp runs from VCC and ground.

circuits.title: Dual-supply output filter
circuits.description: A second-order Butterworth low-pass in the multiple-feedback arrangement for a split-supply system, built on an OPA2134 with its non-inverting input at ground. VIN is a DAC output; R1 feeds the node with C2 to ground and R2 back from the op amp output, R3 runs from that node into the inverting input, and C1 goes from output to inverting input. Gain is –R2/R1. R4 sits in series with the output.

operation.text: Serial audio enters an audio port, passes a 4x/8x oversampling digital filter with the function controls (attenuation, mute, de-emphasis), then an enhanced multilevel delta-sigma modulator driving one DAC per channel. Each DAC is followed by an output amplifier with a low-pass filter. A system clock manager runs from SCK; a zero detector drives the flag pins.

SCK clocks the interpolation filters and modulators. Ratios of 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768 and 1152 fS are accepted, with pulse high and low times of at least 7 ns. Low-jitter, low-noise clocking gives the best performance; TI's PLL170x multiclock generators can supply it.

The modulator rate follows the system clock: 64x for 512, 768 or 1152 fS, 32x for 256 or 384 fS, 16x for 128 or 192 fS. On PCM1780/82 the OVER bit doubles it (128x, 64x, 32x), recommended when fS is at most 24, 48 or 96 kHz respectively.

With the clock running, reset starts once VCC passes about 3 V (2.2 V to 3.7 V) and lasts 3072 system clocks; the outputs sit at VCOM (VCC/2) meanwhile. Registers are loaded with defaults in the next 1/fS, after which correct output follows with the filter's group delay, provided SCK, BCK and LRCK keep running. A soft reset through SRST behaves the same but lasts 1024 system clocks and reloads all registers.

LRCK, BCK and DATA form the audio input. Data is shifted in on BCK rising edges; LRCK runs at fS and BCK at 32, 48 or 64 fS, both synchronous with SCK and ideally divided from it. If LRCK changes or SCK or BCK stops for three bit clocks or more, the part halts and then resynchronises by itself within 3/fS once all three clocks are back; no external reset is needed.

PCM1780/82 accept right-justified 16, 18, 20 or 24 bit, I2S and left-justified (16 to 24 bit), chosen by FMT[2:0]; default is 24-bit left-justified. PCM1781 takes I2S (16 to 24 bit) or 16-bit right-justified, chosen by its FMT pin. All data is two's complement, MSB first. Right- and left-justified frames have LRCK high for the left channel; I2S has it low for the left channel.

A channel whose data stays at zero for 1024 consecutive samples is flagged. On PCM1780/82 each channel has its own flag pin (ZEROL pin 1, ZEROR pin 16), active high by default; ZREV inverts them and AZRO makes pin 16 a combined flag and leaves pin 1 unassigned. PCM1782's flags are open drain. PCM1781 has one combined flag, ZEROA, set when both channels have been zero for 1024 samples. Uses include driving an external mute or reporting to a controller.

PCM1780/82 registers are written over MS (select), MC (clock) and MD (data), independent of the audio clocks. Each write is a 16-bit word: a 0, the 7-bit register index IDX[6:0], then 8 data bits D[7:0], MSB first. MS goes low, 16 MC clocks shift the word in, and MS returning high latches it. The port only writes.

Each channel has its own attenuator: 0 to –63 dB in 0.5 dB steps (DAMS = 0) or 0 to –100 dB in 1 dB steps (DAMS = 1), plus mute. A new level is approached one step every 8/fS. Soft mute (MUTx) ramps the attenuator down to mute at the same rate and back up to the programmed level on release, avoiding clicks.
Setting DACx = 1 parks that output at VCOM (VCC/2). DREV inverts the analog output phase.

Digital de-emphasis for 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz is turned on by DM12 with the rate picked by DMF[1:0] on PCM1780/82, or by DEMP1/DEMP0 on PCM1781. FLT selects sharp (default) or slow rolloff on PCM1780/82.

VOUTL and VOUTR are single-ended outputs centred on 0.5 VCC; each delivers a typical 3.9 Vp-p when loaded by 5 kΩ through a coupling capacitor. The on-chip output amplifier includes an RC continuous-time filter for out-of-band modulator noise, but for many uses it does not remove enough; a further low-pass stage outside the chip is required.
VCOM (pin 13) is the unbuffered VCC/2 reference, brought out for a decoupling capacitor (10 µF electrolytic). It may bias external stages directly, or through a follower when several nodes load it.

The recommended post filters are second-order Butterworth multiple-feedback low-pass stages, single-supply (biased from VCOM) or dual-supply; the MFB form is chosen for low sensitivity to component tolerance and temperature. Application note SBAA055 covers their design.

VCC takes a 0.1 µF ceramic and a 10 µF electrolytic, VCOM 10 µF, output coupling 4.7 µF to 10 µF. Series resistors of 22 Ω to 100 Ω on SCK, LRCK, BCK and DATA form, with board and pin capacitance, a low-pass that cuts emissions and damps ringing.

Use a ground plane split between analog and digital areas, and face the chip's digital pins toward the split so digital lines stay short. Feed the analog and digital sections from separate supplies; where one 5 V supply is shared, put an RF choke or ferrite bead between the digital and analog 5 V.
